Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old man with 3 days of frequent watery diarrhea, intermittent lower central abdominal crampy pain, nausea with one episode of vomiting, and subjective fever; clinician impression: likely gastroenteritis with risk of dehydration; advised oral rehydration, symptomatic treatment, and follow-up if not improved in 48 hours.

History:
- Presenting complaint: several days of profuse watery diarrhea and crampy abdominal pain.
- Timeline:
  - Symptom onset approximately 3 days prior to consultation.
  - Diarrhea described as very watery, occurring approximately hourly while awake.
  - Intermittent crampy abdominal pain, onset coinciding with need to defecate; pain comes and goes.
  - One episode of vomiting after ingesting milk during the illness.
  - Reports feeling hot/feverish but no temperature measurement performed.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Milk ingestion appears to trigger nausea/vomiting for patient.
  - Drinking fluids is tolerated but seems to "pass straight through."
  - No specific relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Nausea and one vomiting episode.
  - Subjective fever/hot sensation; no measured temperature.
  - Urine output reported as somewhat less frequent but "OK."
  - No visible blood in stools per patient.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - Patient denies noticing blood in stool.
  - No other systemic symptoms documented (no documented measured fever, no documented respiratory symptoms).

Past Medical History:
- Patient reports otherwise fit and well; no chronic medical conditions mentioned.
- No regular medications reported.
- Family history: father has colon cancer (patient reports stage III; details not verified).

Medications:
- Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented (taken intermittently for symptoms).
- Diarolyte/Dioralyte (oral rehydration solution) recommended OTC — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No regular prescriptions reported.

Allergies:
- Patient reports no known medication allergies.

Social History:
- Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with him.
- Employment: works in an office in Central London (government).
- Tobacco: occasional/social smoker (e.g., on Fridays); not daily.
- Alcohol: occasional use; heavier drinking once or twice per month when socializing.
- No other substance use documented.
- Reports reluctance to take time off work despite illness.

Family History:
- Father with colon cancer (patient believes stage III; limited details provided).
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- Vitals: none documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results documented or ordered during the consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute watery diarrhea — suspected gastroenteritis
  - Assessment: Clinician impression = gastroenteritis (basic infection of the gut); likely to settle over next few days.
  - Plan:
    - Maintain adequate oral fluids.
    - Use oral rehydration solution (Diarolyte/Dioralyte) available OTC to replace fluids/electrolytes.
    - Soft bland diet (clear fluids initially, then soup, mashed foods, gradually advance as tolerated).
    - Avoid alcohol.
    - Return / contact clinician if symptoms do not settle within 48 hours or if signs of dehydration develop.
- Issue 2: Abdominal crampy pain and feverishness
  - Assessment: Intermittent lower central crampy abdominal pain (patient-rated approximately 6/10 when present); subjective fever.
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic analgesia: Paracetamol appropriate for pain/fever (patient already taking; dose not documented).
    - Monitor temperature if concerns.
- Issue 3: Nausea and vomiting
  - Assessment: Nausea with at least one vomiting episode, apparently triggered by milk.
  - Plan:
    - Avoid milk if it provokes vomiting.
    - Prioritize rehydration with clear fluids and ORS.
    - Seek further care if vomiting persists or prevents oral intake.
- General plan / safety-netting:
  - If signs of dehydration (worsening oliguria, dizziness, inability to tolerate fluids) or lack of improvement within 48 hours, arrange further evaluation and investigations (e.g., assessment for dehydration, possible stool studies or blood tests) — clinician to be contacted.
  - No prescription medications initiated during this consult; OTC ORS and paracetamol recommended.

  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate) not documented.
  - Physical abdominal examination not documented.
  - Stool testing, blood tests, or other investigations not performed or ordered in the transcript.
  - Exact doses, routes, and frequencies for paracetamol and ORS not documented.
  - More detailed clarification of father's cancer (verification) not available.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None clinically significant identified (no direct contradictions in symptom timeline or findings).
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio largely intelligible though video connection was poor; occasional brief interruptions and minor conversational filler present but overall clinical information clear.
